mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last two quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 declined over the last two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) over the last month indicates a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates a robust housing sector.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase & RSAFS decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST increased and RSAFS decreased in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200k and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over the last two months signals a potential deflationary environment, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL decreased by more than 0.5% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75% within the last quarter, coupled with a decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the last month, signals a tightening monetary policy and weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.75% in 3 months & RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.75% in the last quarter and RSAFS decreased by more than 1% in the last month.
